questions.problem:
$$
(P∨Q)⇔Q\,≡\,\bbox[3pt,white,border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAAAAAA}}∧[Q⇒(P∨Q)]
$$

What expression should be inserted into the blank space above to give logically equivalent statements?
questions.worked_solution:
According to the definition of the biconditional, 

- $A⇔B$ is true if $A⇒B$ **and** $B⇒A.$ Otherwise, it is false.

- In other words, $A⇔B$ is true if $A$ and $B$ have the same truth values. Otherwise, it is false.

So in this case, we have

$$
(P∨Q)⇔Q≡[\,(P∨Q)⇒Q]∧[Q⇒(P∨Q)].
$$

Therefore, the missing part is $(P∨Q)⇒Q.$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we use the definition of the biconditional statement to write the equivalence as a conjunction of implications: 

$$
¬(A⇔¬B)≡¬[(A⇒¬B)∧(¬B⇒A)]
$$

Now, we represent all the implications using disjunctions and negations:

$$
¬[(A⇒¬B)∧(¬B⇒A)]≡¬[(¬A∨¬B)∧(¬¬B∨A)]
$$

Next, we use De Morgan's laws:

$$
\begin{aligned}¬[(¬A∨¬B)∧(¬¬B∨A)] & ≡¬(¬A∨¬B)∨¬(¬¬B∨A) \\  & ≡(¬¬A∧¬¬B)∨(¬¬¬B∧¬A)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify the double negations:

$$
(¬¬A∧¬¬B)∨(¬¬¬B∧¬A)≡(A∧B)∨(¬B∧¬A)
$$
